strongest_opposing_case: The released-code mode is known not to contain true SCEVAN tumour calls, so requiring agreement with it may be overly conservative and can preserve a software defect as a gatekeeper.
omitted_facts_that_could_change_the_deci: No barcode-linked scDNA, genotype, CITE-seq, or matched flow identity label is available for these cells.
All three retrospective identity algorithms still derive from the same RNA matrix.
The corrected SCEVAN mode passes all three patients, but that result was obtained after discovering the released-code semantic defect.
optimistic_assumptions: Exact Python-to-R parity on patient5 and patient12 transfers to patient6.
Reported scRNA blast percentages are sufficiently comparable with the ensemble malignant fraction.
RNA-derived CNA methods distinguish malignant from reactive states in these R/R AML samples.
irreversible_cost: Unblinding drug outcomes after a disputed identity definition would contaminate the intended frozen challenge and make a clean prospective test harder.
worst_consequence: A normal or reactive state could be treated as a leukemic state and produce a spurious patient-specific drug vulnerability claim.
strongest_supporting_evidence: The corrected implementation matches native R SCEVAN exactly for every evaluable cell in both reference patients, completes all 11652 cells across the three patients, and reduces blast-fraction discrepancies without changing thresholds.
neutral_verdict: Keep monotherapy unblinding locked under the preregistered dual-mode sensitivity rule. Treat the corrected result as a successful computational repair and a strong rationale for orthogonal identity collection, not as final identity proof.
largest_unknown: Whether corrected RNA-derived malignant and normal calls agree with barcode-linked genomic or orthogonal immunophenotypic identity.
evidence_that_would_reverse_the_verdict: Barcode-linked scDNA or genotype concordance for major virtual states.
Matched CITE-seq or flow labels plus an AML-specific reference call under the frozen strict identity thresholds.
A prospectively registered independent replication of the corrected identity and drug-direction challenge.
